overview: Rightmove operates the UK's largest online property portal, connecting consumers searching for homes to buy or rent with estate agents, new homes developers, and other property-related partners who pay subscription fees to advertise. The business is a pure-play UK digital classifieds/marketplace model with no physical property exposure, generating very high margins (underlying operating margin ~70%) from a capital-light platform. Rightmove operates solely in the UK, with offices in Milton Keynes, London and Newcastle, and has expanded beyond core Agency/New Homes listings into strategic growth areas: Commercial Property, Financial Services (mortgages) and Rental Services.

business_model.summary: Rightmove earns B2B subscription/membership fees from property professionals (estate agents, new homes developers, commercial agents, mortgage brokers) for advertising on its platform, which is free to consumers. Revenue is driven by Average Revenue Per Advertiser (ARPA) growth via package upgrades and incremental product purchases, rather than membership/customer count growth, which has been broadly flat to low-single-digit. FY2025 revenue was £425.1m, up 9% YoY (Agency +9% to £304.7m, New Homes +9% to £75.3m, Other/strategic growth areas +11% to £45.1m).

revenue_streams.name: New Homes (developers)
revenue_streams.trend: growing but membership declining; ARPA offsetting (+9% revenue FY2025 despite -1% membership)

revenue_streams.name: Other / Strategic Growth Areas (Commercial Property, Financial Services/Mortgages, Rental Services, Data, Overseas)
revenue_streams.trend: fast growing, +25% FY2025, management targets 20-30% in 2026

business_model.customer_type: B2B subscription model: ~19,272 members (16,385 agency branches, 2,887 new homes developments, plus commercial/mortgage partners) as of FY2025; no customer represents more than 3% of Group revenue (diversified base). End consumers use the platform free of charge.
business_model.geographic_mix: 100% UK — no international revenue exposure (domestic property portal only).

main_competitors: OnTheMarket (acquired by CoStar Group, Dec 2023, for ~£100m)
REA Group (Australia/News Corp, made unsolicited takeover bids for Rightmove in 2024)
competitive_position.market_position: Clear UK market leader: over 80% of all time spent on UK property portals in 2025 was on Rightmove (2024: 83%), per Comscore/SimilarWeb data cited in FY2025 annual report; 96% home-mover brand awareness; over 85% of traffic is direct/organic (not paid or referred).

moat_factors.description: Two-sided marketplace: largest consumer audience (>8m enhanced consumer profiles, c.19,000 core partners) attracts agents who need the most eyeballs on listings, which in turn attracts more consumers. 25+ years of compounding first-party data (>90% proprietary) reinforces this.

Agency membership retention running at ~90% annually (second-highest in 10 years in FY2025; 96% in H1 2026, highest in >10 years), reflecting embeddedness of Rightmove leads in agents' workflows and CRM integrations.
96% home-mover brand awareness; most searches for property in the UK begin with 'Rightmove' rather than generic terms per Google data cited by management.

25 years of proprietary UK property/consumer/partner data (>68bn consumer signals, >100m historical listings, c.10,000 properties uploaded daily) feeding AI-driven products (vendor propensity models, valuation tools) that are difficult for newer entrants to replicate quickly.

moat_factors.factor: Low capital intensity / high cash conversion
moat_factors.description: Capex is minimal (~£10m/yr on ~£425m revenue); operating cash flow ran at 107% of operating profit in FY2025, enabling heavy shareholder returns, though this is a financial strength rather than a true competitive barrier.
Low barriers to entry into online property advertising; management explicitly flags 'high returns and low entry barriers' as a principal competitive risk in its own risk disclosures.

weaknesses: Single-country revenue concentration (100% UK) with no geographic diversification to offset a UK housing downturn

CoStar's well-funded backing of OnTheMarket represents the first time a UK portal competitor has institutional-scale capital (CoStar reportedly committed to spend many multiples of OnTheMarket's historical marketing budget, and more than Rightmove's total annual marketing spend)
Historically high pricing/margins (quoted ~68-70% operating margins) make Rightmove a visible target for undercutting by rivals offering agents lower-cost advertising
New Homes segment structurally exposed to UK housebuilding volumes, which remain depressed versus historic norms
Low barriers to entry acknowledged by the company itself in risk disclosures

growth_drivers: ARPA growth via package upgrades (Optimiser Edge / Ascend top-tier packages) and incremental product purchases above monthly commitment thresholds (52% of agents spent above commitment in FY2025)

Strategic growth areas (Commercial Property, Financial Services/Mortgages, Rental Services) growing 20-30% targeted for 2026, now ~7% of group revenue and contributing double-digit share of incremental revenue growth

AI-powered product rollout (31 AI initiatives underway at FY2025 year-end; £60m committed AI/innovation investment programme for 2026-2028) spanning consumer search/engagement (AI Keywords, Style with AI) and partner tools (Opportunity Manager, Online Agent Valuation)

New Homes recovery optionality: management frames the current New Homes weakness as a volume headwind that should normalize/recover as housebuilding activity picks up, with ARPA still growing strongly even as unit volumes fall

Structural UK housing tailwinds: population growth of ~450k/year versus only ~200k new home starts/year, an aging housing stock requiring modernization, and ongoing digitization of an analogue industry
Falling UK interest/mortgage rates through 2025-2026 supporting a gradual recovery in housing transaction volumes (1.2m in FY2025 vs 1.1m in FY2024, against a long-run average of ~1.2m)
Capital allocation optionality for bolt-on M&A alongside continued buybacks/dividends

business.description: CoStar acquired OnTheMarket (Dec 2023, ~£100m) and committed to a multi-year, well-funded marketing and investment campaign explicitly aimed at disrupting Rightmove's and Zoopla's share; CoStar's CEO has publicly called Rightmove 'complacent' and highlighted its high margins as vulnerable to price competition.

Press speculation about a possible CoStar acquisition of Zoopla (whose owner ZPG/Silver Lake has explored strategic options) could create a single, better-capitalized #2 challenger with combined OnTheMarket+Zoopla scale.

New Homes membership has been declining (-1% FY2025, developments at lowest new-to-market rate on record per H1 2026 presentation) as housebuilders constrain new site openings; FY2026 guidance for New Homes development volumes was cut to a 6-10% decline.

Management flags that AI search tools could change how consumers discover and interact with property brands, potentially bypassing portals, though currently <0.5% of Rightmove traffic originates from LLM referrals.
Company's own risk disclosure acknowledges the online property advertising market has 'high returns and low entry barriers,' inviting new entrants.

financial.risk: New leverage via £200m revolving credit facility
financial.description: Rightmove has historically operated debt-free; in July 2026 it introduced a new £200m RCF to help fund an enhanced buyback programme (>£400m of capital returns targeted over the 12 months to July 2027), marking a shift from its pure cash-funded capital return policy.
Heavy reliance on buybacks (£141.1m in FY2025, 3% of shares outstanding) to drive EPS growth could mask slower underlying profit growth if buyback pace moderates.

regulatory.risk: UK Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act / CMA scrutiny
regulatory.description: As the dominant UK property portal, Rightmove is explicitly named in its own risk disclosures as subject to the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act, which could in principle lead to conduct requirements given its market position, similar to how DMA/DMCCA-style rules have affected Big Tech platforms.

regulatory.risk: Renters' Rights Act and other property-sector regulation
regulatory.description: Changes to UK lettings/rental regulation could affect agent partners' business models and indirectly affect Rightmove's Rental Services revenue and lettings membership.
Financial Services (mortgage) offerings bring Rightmove under FCA rules, adding compliance risk as this growth area scales.

macro.description: Revenue is correlated with UK housing transaction volumes and agent/developer marketing budgets; a severe and prolonged recession could shrink the customer base, though management notes the business model has proven resilient through past downturns (e.g., 2008 GFC, COVID) given the subscription (not pay-per-listing) model.

UK mortgage rates directly affect transaction volumes and consumer affordability; FY2025/H1 2026 saw early-stage recovery as rates fell, but this reversed somewhat in H2 2025 amid budget-related uncertainty.
UK Budget announcements (e.g., November 2025 budget) created buyer/investor hesitation and paused transaction decisions in H2 2025, illustrating sensitivity to fiscal policy news flow.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: UK residential property market (~$12trn) and 4th-largest global commercial property market, with resale transactions at a long-run floor of ~0.9-1.2m/year; 2025 saw 1.2m transactions (10% up YoY) as interest rates fell, broadly back to the long-run average. Structural housing shortage (population +450k/yr vs ~200k new homes/yr) and an aging housing stock support long-term digitization and transaction tailwinds.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high indirect cyclicality via UK housing transaction volumes and agent/developer marketing budgets, but historically resilient relative to transaction volumes because Rightmove's subscription model does not require a completed transaction to earn revenue — agents pay to advertise regardless of deal flow.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate indirect sensitivity: UK mortgage/base rates affect buyer affordability, transaction volumes, and housebuilder new-site openings (New Homes segment), with falling rates in 2025-2026 providing a modest tailwind.
key_input_costs: Technology/cloud hosting and AI infrastructure costs
Payroll (average headcount +5% and salary inflation ~4% in FY2025)

recent_developments.event: Rightmove's board unanimously rejected a series of increasingly sweetened takeover proposals from Australia's REA Group (News Corp-backed), ultimately valuing Rightmove at up to ~£6.1bn; REA withdrew its bid shortly after, citing the board's unwillingness to engage.

CoStar Group's ~£100m acquisition of OnTheMarket (completed Dec 2023/early 2024) continues to be the dominant competitive narrative; CoStar has committed to multi-year, outsized sales and marketing spend aimed at taking UK portal share from both Rightmove and Zoopla, though impact on Rightmove's core partner/consumer metrics remained limited through FY2025 per the company's own risk disclosure.

FY2025 annual results: revenue +9% to £425.1m, underlying operating profit +9% to £297.7m, underlying EPS +11% to 29.1p; strategic growth areas (Commercial, Mortgages, Rental Services) grew 25% combined to £29.1m (7% of group revenue); £219.7m returned to shareholders via buybacks and dividends.
Company confirmed FY2026 guidance alongside a trading update / AGM (per Radiocor/Borsa Italiana coverage), ahead of the subsequent H1 cut in July.

H1 2026 results: revenue +7% to £225.8m; Agency +9%, New Homes +2% (volume headwind), Strategic Growth Areas +14% in H1 (on track for 20-30% full-year growth, more than double H1 pace in H2). Management CUT full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance to 6-8% (from 8-10%) due to weaker New Homes development volumes (developments expected down 6-10% YoY), while MAINTAINING underlying operating profit growth guidance of 3-5% and underlying EPS growth guidance of 'at least 5%.' Announced enhanced capital returns of >£400m over the 12 months to July 2027 (including ~£330m of buybacks), partly funded by a new £200m revolving credit facility — the company's first meaningful use of debt financing.
Agency H1 retention hit a >10-year high of 96%; New Homes developments coming to market at the lowest rate on record, reflecting ongoing housebuilder caution.

items.notes: Cut from previous 8-10% guidance, reflecting weaker New Homes development volumes (developments expected to decline 6-10% YoY) even as ARPA and Agency growth remain strong.
Held despite the revenue guidance cut, implying cost discipline and mix benefits offsetting the New Homes shortfall.
Supported by continued share buybacks reducing the share count alongside profit growth.
Commercial Property, Financial Services, Rental Services combined; H2 2026 growth rate expected to be more than double the H1 rate.
Enhanced versus prior capital return pace; includes ~£330m of share buybacks, partly funded by a new £200m revolving credit facility (first notable use of debt).
Reflects subdued housebuilder new-site openings; New Homes ARPA growth continues to partially offset volume decline.

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Johan Svanstrom and CFO Ruaridh Hook characterized H1 2026 as delivering 'strong business and product results for partners and consumers,' citing record Agency retention (96%, a >10-year high) and Strategic Growth Areas 'on track for 20-30% growth.' New Homes was explicitly flagged as 'a volume headwind today but will recover.' Management emphasized continued technology/AI investment (£60m committed 2026-2028) is 'already delivering strong results' and framed the business as building toward an 'agentic-powered property marketplace.'

bull_case: Dominant, durable network-effect moat evidenced by >80% share of UK property-portal time spent and ~90-96% agency retention rates, with limited measurable impact from CoStar/OnTheMarket competition on core metrics through H1 2026

Extremely high-margin (c.68-70% underlying operating margin), capital-light, highly cash-generative subscription model with no debt-funded operations historically and strong free cash flow conversion (107% of operating profit in FY2025)
ARPA-led growth model has repeatedly offset flat-to-declining membership counts (especially in New Homes), demonstrating pricing power and depth of partner value even in soft market segments
Diversification into higher-growth strategic growth areas (Commercial, Mortgages, Rental Services growing 20-30%) provides a second growth engine beyond the core Agency/New Homes subscription base
Structural UK housing supply shortage and falling interest rates provide multi-year tailwinds for transaction volumes and partner monetization as the market normalizes
bear_case: CoStar's well-capitalized, explicitly aggressive multi-year assault on UK portal share via OnTheMarket represents the first genuinely well-funded competitive threat in Rightmove's history, with management's own risk disclosures acknowledging 'low entry barriers' and 'increased competition'

FY2026 revenue guidance was already cut once (8-10% to 6-8%) due to New Homes weakness, raising questions about the durability of growth if housebuilding activity does not recover as management expects

Introduction of a £200m revolving credit facility to fund buybacks marks a shift away from Rightmove's historically pristine, debt-free balance sheet, potentially signalling EPS growth is increasingly reliant on financial engineering rather than organic profit growth

100% UK revenue concentration leaves no geographic diversification to cushion a renewed UK housing downturn driven by rates, fiscal policy (e.g., budget-related uncertainty seen in H2 2025), or recession

High historical valuation multiples and premium margins make the stock vulnerable to de-rating if competitive, regulatory (DMCCA), or AI-disruption risks crystallize, as reflected in a wide dispersion of analyst price targets and at least one major bank (Citigroup) issuing a sell recommendation following the OnTheMarket/CoStar deal
